name: Fibromuscular Dysplasia of the Visceral Arteries

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No formal standardized criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and clinical presentation

criteria.description: Characteristic 'string of beads' appearance on angiography of visceral arteries
Exclusion of atherosclerotic disease and vasculitis by clinical and laboratory evaluation
Symptoms consistent with visceral artery ischemia or aneurysm such as abdominal pain or hypertension

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic angiographic findings plus exclusion of other causes such as atherosclerosis and vasculitis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging modalities and clinical correlation; biopsy is rarely performed.

pathognomonic.symptomName: String of beads appearance on visceral artery angiography
searchTerms: beaded pattern on abdominal artery imaging
string of beads in visceral arteries

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visceral artery stenosis leading to ischemic abdominal pain
searchTerms: abdominal pain from poor blood flow
pain due to visceral artery narrowing

common.symptomName: Hypertension secondary to renal artery involvement
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney artery
secondary high blood pressure from kidneys

common.notes: Audible vascular murmur over affected arteries

searchTerms: stomach upset from poor blood flow
nausea due to intestinal blood loss

common.symptomName: Weight loss due to chronic mesenteric ischemia
searchTerms: unintentional weight loss from chronic gut blood flow problems
losing weight due to poor intestinal circulation
weight loss related to long-term gut ischemia

occasional.notes: May be asymptomatic or cause complications
Due to arterial stenosis or occlusion

searchTerms: artery wall split in abdominal vessels
intestinal tissue death from lack of blood
bowel damage due to blood loss

rare.symptomName: Hepatic artery involvement causing liver ischemia
searchTerms: liver ischemia due to artery involvement

laboratory: Renal function tests may be abnormal if renal arteries involved
imaging: Catheter-based angiography showing 'string of beads' appearance
CT angiography and MR angiography demonstrating arterial stenosis and aneurysms
Doppler ultrasound showing abnormal flow in affected arteries
genetic: No definitive genetic mutation identified; possible familial clustering reported
other: Histopathology (rarely performed) shows medial fibroplasia and arterial wall thickening

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of traditional cardiovascular risk factors
Diffuse plaque formation rather than focal 'string of beads'
Elevated inflammatory markers absent in FMD
Systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss
Histopathologic evidence of vessel wall inflammation

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe abdominal pain indicating possible artery dissection
Signs of bowel ischemia such as bloody diarrhea or peritonitis
Rapidly worsening hypertension refractory to treatment
references: Olin JW, Gornik HL, Bacharach JM, et al. Fibromuscular Dysplasia: State of the Science and Critical Unanswered Questions: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association. Circulation. 2014;129(9):1048-1078.
